text: The shapes and the open values of this slice are read as follows and written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: the raise is POST /approvals on /api/recovery/decision/v1 with a body carrying caseId, decisionCode, regulationItem, capabilityArea, productGroup, amount, sourceType, sourceRef, ruleId, ruleVersion and an Idempotency-Key; ApprovalAction carries a status and a reason of at most 1,000 characters; ApprovalPage and DecisionLogPage carry items, page, size and total; the final call of a routing record and of a decision is read as a value of the final-call list of the reference data with the version in force, the values APPROVED, RETURNED and REFUSED being the three decisions of T-A.1 and TSD P7 v2 T3.2; the decision code of the escalation and of the sale selection is read as a value of LOV-DECISION with the version in force; the base value of escalation_level, the due time of an item and the page size are read from configuration and not written in code; the texts of MSG-P7-009, MSG-P7-010 and MSG-P7-011 are left as identifiers because no source writes them; and the approval queue is described without a panel id.
why: TSD P7 v2 names ApprovalPage, ApprovalDetail, ApprovalAction, DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without a field set and publishes no operation that creates an approval, the content of LOV-DECISION is not enumerated in any source this story may read, final_call has no list, and the texts of three message identifiers are never written out; inventing any of them would put a value into the build that no owner approved.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 approval and decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-PRODUCT, T-A.1 API-P7-002 to API-P7-008, T-A.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.15, A2.16, A2.18, A2.23 and A2.24; legacy RWB-E6-028 Endpoints, Screen and states and Validation and messages; the Ownership Map api rows to P7
confirm: P7 solution architect and the API specification owner at the contract baseline of wave 4, with the message standard owner for the three texts
impact: The request and answer of the eight operations and the final calls of the two records; a later change is a contract version and a reference-data load, not a rewrite of the criteria

text: The database login of the capability is the per-service login of DP-02 and the story calls it 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)'; no login name is written in the story, in a migration or in a test, and the shared login of the legacy module is never named.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives every service its own login but no source fixes the login name of rwb-decision, and a guessed name would become a credential in a script.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-02; the sibling P7 stories RWB-P7-E2028-APP and RWB-P7-E2024-APP section 1
confirm: ACE DB team at the schema and login allocation of wave 1 (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the P7 DB story)
impact: One identifier in the migration and the deployment values; nothing else in the story or the tests depends on it

text: The 'limit exceeded' of legacy AC2 and of rule R-WO-12 is read as the write-off committee limit the rule names, tested by rwb-writeoff and never by this service, and the level the pack is routed at is the approval_level value of the P4 delegation answer for decision D9, the regulation item, the product group, the amount and the business date. This service stores the level, the delegation row id and the limit version and re-computes no limit, holds no delegation row and compares no amount.
why: The legacy text says only 'limit exceeded' and names no level, no item and no version, while TSD P7 v2 A2.24 and FSD P7 v3 A2.15 read the level from the versioned delegation table at the moment of the decision and the Ownership Map puts that table with P4; a computed level in P7 would be a second authority beside the DoA table.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-028 AC2 and the Data table; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12; FSD P7 v3 A2.15 and A2.24; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-038 to DF-DEC-040 and T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL; the Ownership Map table delegation_limit to P4 and api row GET /doa-limits; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41
confirm: P4 rwb-access and the P7 solution architect at the delegation contract baseline
impact: The routing of every escalated pack and the version recorded on it; a delegation change is a P4 load and not a release of this service

text: The decision code of the escalation record and of the sale-selection record is read as a value of LOV-DECISION for the write-off decision D9 with the version in force, and is never a constant of this service; the rule version of the two rows is the version of the rule package in force on the business date, read from the registry and from the entry, and no version label is written in the story, because the label of the write-off package in force is not fixed by any source.
why: TSD P7 v2 DF-DEC-003 types decision_code as varchar(8) against LOV-DECISION without enumerating it, and TSD P7 v2 DF-DEC-005 carries rule_version as text with no label; the value is reference data and the label is a fact of the registry, so writing either in code would freeze a business value.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 and DF-DEC-005; FSD P7 v3 A2.16.3.2 field catalog (decision codes D5.1 to D9.3); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 route set Write-off, decision D9, rows R-WO-12 and R-WO-32; Architecture v5 slide 27; Temporal design slide 15

confirm: Rule owner RW-COE and the reference-data administrator at the registry and list baseline
impact: The code and the version on every write-off entry; a package promotion changes the resolved version and not the code of this service

text: One escalation is read as two ledger entries and not as one. rwb-writeoff writes the local record of R-WO-12 with the state change and publishes it on rwb.decision-record.v1, and rwb-decision writes the routing record of the approval it raises; both are collected into the central ledger, each names the same case and the same rule and neither repeats the other's facts, and the ledger read returns them in chain order so the pair reads as one step. The same reading applies to R-WO-32 and the sale selection.
why: Architecture v5 slide 20 makes the record local to the service that acts and slide 28 collects it centrally, while FSD P7 v3 A2.15 makes the routing of an item its own entry with the rule, the version and the route parameter; a choice of one reading alone would either lose the routing facts or suppress the state record the ledger exists for.

applied_in: RWB-P7-E6028-APP sections 4 steps 7, 9 and 13, 7 (AC1, AC8), 8 (BR4, BR10) and 9

impact: The count of entries per action in the ITG run report; a duplicate and a pair are told apart by the record source and the chain order

text: The two platform H dependencies the DP table adds, H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON from DP-03 and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON from DP-19, are platform CON stories of wave 0, and the four consumed contracts the metadata does not carry — the P4 delegation answer, the P4 authorise answer, the P3 case read and the reference-data list values — are published contracts or fakes. None of the six blocks the build, so Ready to start stays Day 1 and the story is built against the fakes from the first day.
why: Template and Rules section R5.7 makes a platform CON story and a C dependency non-blocking, and R5.4 keeps an H to the same service or to a platform CON story; the metadata rows name None and RWB-S7-E6028-CON only, so the six must be carried somewhere other than the two rows.

confirm: Delivery lead at the wave 4 dependency review
impact: The Day-1 allocation of the lane; a platform contract that slips would show in the fake swap of every story of the key, not only in this one

text: The approval read and the three decisions declare the Decision log right A of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and, in addition, the capability area WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING carried on the approval row; the FSD P7 v3 T6.1 column is read as the right of the two ledger reads and not as the right of the approval operations; and the credit approval committee member RW-CREDCOMM is read as a holder of that capability right because R-WO-12 routes the pack to that committee, although the legacy permission table of RWB-E6-028 does not list the role.
why: The same technical specification declares A on the approval operations and lists only R for every role, and the legacy story guards the same actions with the write-off capability area at right A; the rule routes the pack to a committee the legacy table does not name, so one reading alone either locks out the committee the rule names or lets a role the legacy table excludes decide.
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1, T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY; legacy RWB-E6-028 Permission checks; FSD P7 v3 A2.16.3.3 and A2.19.3.3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12
confirm: P4 rwb-access security administrator and the P7 business analyst, at the role model review of wave 1
impact: Who may decide an escalated write-off pack; a wrong reading either blocks the committee or grants a right the legacy table withholds
